idiom_name: MarshalXML on the domain type (xml.Encoder to an io.Writer)
implementation_notes: encoding/xml provides marshalling, not a transformation engine: the Transformer becomes a type implementing xml.Marshaler - MarshalXML(e *xml.Encoder, start xml.StartElement) error - that encodes tokens per element with EncodeToken/EncodeElement, or a plain function writing escaped text to an io.Writer. Struct tags cover the mechanical cases, but conditional attributes, nested lists and mixed content require MarshalXML or manual token emission; the standard library has no XSLT, and html/template is Template View, not Transform View.
pitfalls: Every start element must be closed with start.End(): omitting the end token yields malformed output that only fails at the consumer.
Text written outside the encoder must be escaped explicitly (html.EscapeString for HTML, xml.EscapeText for XML); raw fmt.Fprintf into markup is the standard injection footgun.
MarshalXML must not retain the encoder or accumulate state between calls: per-request state belongs to a fresh Encoder or to the value being marshalled.
